reason: This text is the opening of the Book of Job (Job 1:1-22 in Hebrew), which introduces Job as a righteous man, describes his wealth and family, and narrates the dialogue between God and Satan regarding Job's faithfulness, followed by a series of disasters that befall him. The passage focuses on Job's individual piety, his suffering, and his faithful response ('The Lord gave, and the Lord has taken away; blessed be the name of the Lord'). There are no Hebrew leaders depicted in this passage, and there is no complaining by any leaders about any people. The main figures are Job himself, his household members, servant messengers reporting disasters, God, and Satan.
